nuclear weapon.gloss: A weapon that derives its energy from the nuclear reactions of either fission or fusion.

nuclear winter.gloss: A predicted drop in global temperature following a nuclear war due to dust in the upper atmosphere reducing sunlight reaching the ground.

nucleic acid.gloss: (biochemistry, genetics) Any acidic, chainlike biological macromolecule consisting of multiple repeat units of phosphoric acid, sugar and purine and pyrimidine bases; they are involved in the preservation, replication and expression of here

nucleotide.gloss: (biochemistry) The monomer constituting DNA or RNA biopolymer molecules. Each nucleotide consists of a nitrogenous heterocyclic base (or nucleobase), which can be either a double-ringed purine or a single-ringed pyrimidine; a five-carbon pe

nucleus.gloss: The core, central part of something, around which other elements are assembled.

nude.gloss: A painting, sculpture, photograph or other artwork or mass-media-reproduced image depicting one or more human figure(s) in a state of near or total undress.

nudge.gloss: (transitive) To push against gently, especially in order to gain attention or give a signal.

nudiustertian.gloss: (rare, obsolete, modern uses probably, _, humorous) Of or relating to the day before yesterday; very recent.

nueva vizcaya.gloss: A province of Cagayan Valley, Luzon, Philippines. Capital: Bayombong.

nugget.gloss: (countable, slang) An inexperienced, newly trained fighter pilot.

nuisance.gloss: (legal) Anything harmful or offensive to the community or to a member of it, for which a legal remedy exists.

nuke.gloss: (transitive, chiefly, US, colloquial, figuratively) To destroy or erase completely.

null.gloss: A non-existent or empty value or set of values.

numazu.gloss: A city in Shizuoka Prefecture, Japan.

numb.gloss: Physically unable to feel, not having the power of sensation.

number.gloss: (countable) An abstract entity used to describe quantity.

number-theoretical.gloss: (mathematics) Of or relating to number theory.

numbers.gloss: The Book of Numbers, the fourth of the Books of Moses in the Old Testament of the Bible, the fourth book in the Torah.

numbers station.gloss: (radio, espionage) A shortwave radio station characterized by unusual broadcasts, often of artificially generated voices reciting streams of numbers, words, etc., supposedly of coded messages.

numeral.gloss: A symbol that is not a word and represents a number, such as the Arabic numerals 1, 2, 3 or the Roman numerals I, V, X, L.
(linguistics) A number word, a simple or compound word for a number often having particular grammatical attributes depending on the language.

numerology.gloss: The study of the purported mystical relationship between numbers (or the letters of words, represented by numbers) and the character or action of physical objects and living beings.

numinous.gloss: Of or relating to a numen (divinity); indicating the presence of a divinity. [from mid 17th c.]

nun.gloss: A member of a Christian religious community of women who live by certain vows and usually wear a habit, (Roman Catholicism, specifically) those living together in a cloister.

nunavut.gloss: A territory in northern Canada. Capital: Iqaluit.

nuncheon.gloss: (now, _, dialectal, archaic) A drink or light snack taken in the afternoon; a refreshment between meals.

nuptial.gloss: Of or pertaining to wedding and marriage.

nur-sultan.gloss: Former name of Astana: the capital city of Kazakhstan, used from 2019 to 2022.

nuremberg.gloss: A major city in Bavaria, Germany.

nurse.gloss: A person involved in providing direct care for the sick:

nursemaid.gloss: A woman or girl employed to care for children.

nursery rhyme.gloss: A short poem or song for children, mostly anonymous or handed down by folklore

nursery school.gloss: (, Canada, British) An educational institution for small children (normally around 3 to 5 years old, who not yet have begun primary school).

nut.gloss: (food, broadly) Any of various hard-shelled seeds or hard, dry fruits from various families of plants.

(hardware) A piece of hardware, typically metal and typically hexagonal or square in shape, with a hole through it having internal screw threads, intended to be screwed onto a threaded bolt or other threaded shaft.
(vulgar, slang, chiefly plural) A testicle, often used in the plural form.

nuthatch.gloss: Any of various small passerine birds from the genus Sitta, found throughout the northern hemisphere and noted for their unusual proclivity for climbing down trees head first.

nutmeg.gloss: The aromatic seed of this tree, used as a spice.
(football, hockey, basketball) The playing of the ball between the legs of an opponent.

nutrient.gloss: A source of nourishment, such as food, that can be metabolized by an organism to give energy and build tissue.

nutritional.gloss: Of, pertaining to, or providing nutrition.

nutritious.gloss: (of food or drink) Providing nutrients; healthy to eat or drink.

nuts.gloss: (colloquial) Crazy, mad; unusually pleased or, alternatively, angered.

nutty.gloss: (slang) Barmy: eccentric, odd; crazy, mad, insane.

nuzzle.gloss: Often followed by in or into: to press or push the nose or snout, mouth, face, etc., against or into someone or something; to touch someone or something with the nose or snout, etc.

nychthemeron.gloss: (uncommon) A period of one day and one night, a date: in the West, a period of 24 consecutive hours.

nylon.gloss: Originally, the DuPont company trade name for polyamide, a copolymer whose molecules consist of alternating diamine and dicarboxylic acid monomers bonded together; now generically used for this type of polymer.

nymph.gloss: (Greek mythology, Roman mythology) Any female nature spirit associated with water, forests, grotto, wind, etc.
A young girl, especially one who is attractive, beautiful or graceful.

née.gloss: Used when giving the maiden name of a woman.
Used when giving a former name. Originally known as.

négligée.gloss: (obsolete) A woman's lightweight gown of the eighteenth century. [18th–19th c.]
